scope: Independent feature/call-path/source review, finite effect/panic/drop probe and relevant driver/CLI/API tests. No performance, full-workspace or product gate.
findings: Cargo resolver confirms timings is absent by default in all four crates and enabling zil-cli/timings enables exactly the intended chain into driver/backend/API.

Without the feature TimingTrace/TimingScope are zero-sized with no Drop implementation. measure/value evaluate their supplied FnOnce once and preserve its return/error/panic and captured-value destruction; the independent probe exercises both compile configurations.
Enabled collector field/clock/parent/unit/Mutex/drop logic is preserved under the module; no safety, ABI, query-key or language-budget change.

CLI rejects an unavailable --timings request with E-CLI-ARGUMENT exit64. Driver checks compile_source, compile_project and compile_path before reading a path or invoking parsing/query/Verify work, returning Driver Unsupported.
Existing collector parent scopes, early errors, actual Verify runs and cache reuse remain covered by enabled tests.
observations: The no-feature configuration error guarantee is no source read or verification; normal report setup and an existing session-capacity eviction guard can still occur before the compile_source/project support check. This is not a claim of literally zero work on an invalid request.
The disabled collector does not remove unrelated existing CompileReport seconds/object receipt timers. Zero-size/drop properties alone do not establish end-to-end performance gain.
Direct TimingTrace users must honor timing::available(); documented driver/CLI entry points reject unavailable requests.
